title: シルクロード ― 言葉と物が旅した道
style: 画風01・光彩のある劇場アニメ背景を基調にした歴史文化ドキュメンタリー
research_basis: UNESCO World Heritage: Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor
UNESCO Silk Roads Programme: merchants, religions, crafts and paper-making

scope.geography: East Asia, Central Asia, the Iranian plateau, Indian subcontinent, Arabian lands, Mediterranean and Europe
scope.time: multiple periods from antiquity through the medieval era; do not imply one simultaneous journey
scope.route_model: a branching network of land and maritime routes linked by oasis cities, caravanserais, passes and ports

visual_anchors.merchant_group: a small 7th-century Sogdian-led relay caravan with Bactrian camels, mixed Central Asian clothing, practical bundles and water skins; used only for the central land-route sequence
visual_anchors.student: the same modern 17-year-old Japanese male high-school student used in H040-H041, navy blazer and white shirt, as the final learner viewpoint

material_accuracy: Bactrian camels have two humps and practical saddles; caravans are modest working groups, not endless fantasy columns
show silk bolts, glass vessels, pepper or spice sacks, coins and metalwork as relay-traded goods from different origins and periods
avoid implying that one merchant travelled directly from Han China to Rome carrying all listed goods
desert routes depend on oasis towns, wells, caravanserais and local guides; mountains require pack animals and seasonal passes
paper-making in Central and Western Asia uses adapted fibres or rags, vats, mould screens, pressing and drying; it changes across regions
history_accuracy: use Silk Roads in the plural and show both land and maritime branches in the opening network
the modern term Silk Road was coined much later; do not show an ancient sign bearing that name
Buddhism's movement from the Indian subcontinent into Central and East Asia involved monks, pilgrims, translators, patrons, texts and art over centuries
Islam's spread into Central Asia involved political change, migration, scholarship and trade; do not present it as a single peaceful caravan event
languages and art are exchanged and transformed locally rather than copied unchanged
paper-making spread through a multi-stage Eurasian process and evolved in Samarkand, Baghdad and later western regions; avoid a single secret-stealing or one-battle origin story
European learning is one later part of the network's legacy, not the sole destination or measure of value

composition.subtitle_safe_area: keep faces, goods, manuscripts, tools and route landmarks above the lower 45 percent
composition.camera: one stable push, pull or hold per shot
composition.text: no readable generated labels, maps, scripts, manuscript passages, coins or signs

avoid: a single straight red line from China to Rome
one giant caravan carrying every culture at once
Arabian Nights fantasy, empty-desert exoticism or generic oriental palace imagery
modern camel saddles, plastic containers, wheeled luggage or tourist clothing
Buddha, mosque and church symbols floating together as a fantasy collage
the Battle of Talas as a simple moment when paper was stolen
readable generated calligraphy, route names, religious texts, logos or watermarks
